items.streamTitle: Election Day glitches and unrelated images were rapidly turned into unverified fraud narratives
items.streamSummary: AP's November 3 case checks separated a genuine New York scanner fault from unverified sabotage claims, disproved a Houston ballot-raid rumor and documented false Georgia polling texts of unknown origin.
items.attribution: Melissa Goldin and Calvin Woodward — Associated Press (original Election Day fact checks)

items.streamTitle: NATO outlined a cross-domain synchronization problem, not a measured capability gain
items.streamSummary: NATO ACT's November 3 report describes four priorities for military–civilian multi-domain coordination across 30 nations. The conference was an implementation forum, not an evaluated improvement in operational effects.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — November 3 official conference report

items.streamTitle: Audit-task LLM agents yielded to some professional pressure but resisted a client inducement
items.streamSummary: Across twelve LLM audit settings, professional authority cues shifted some agent judgments without new evidence, while client career inducements often reduced revision. The behavior is not validated as human conformity.
items.attribution: Richard Zhe Wang — arXiv preprint (delegated-audit agent experiment)

items.streamTitle: Eye-tracking-informed cues improved some immersive 3D network-analysis judgments
items.streamSummary: A 2026 IEEE paper used VR eye tracking to study 3D network analysis and derive visual cues that improved correctness in most follow-up trials. Real-world analytic transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Wang et al. — IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (VR eye-tracking studies)

items.streamTitle: A 500-million-persona synthetic economy emphasized the gap between scale and behavioral validity
items.streamSummary: S²-MAS reported 500 million synthetic household personas and 12 million simulated agents, with explicit decision/state separation. Its model's 38.37% macro F1 and absence of prospective policy tests constrain behavioral claims.
items.attribution: Li et al. — arXiv preprint (survey-grounded economic multi-agent framework)

items.streamTitle: Relationally persuasive AI increased both helpful reliance and harmful overreliance
items.streamSummary: A randomized 462-adult study found relational AI framing increased reliance on both correct and incorrect advice. Accuracy sensitivity and the proposed trust mechanism remain unproven.
items.attribution: Mizrak, Kirgiz and Demirel — Journal of Intelligence (randomized experiment)

items.streamTitle: Self-evolving agent evaluations caught regressions hidden by final benchmark scores
items.streamSummary: SEAGym separated agent-harness validation, held-out transfer and replay. An intermediate snapshot collapsed to 6/80 solved tasks, revealing a regression that final scores hid.
items.attribution: Zheng et al. — arXiv preprint (SEAGym agent evaluation)

items.streamTitle: Higher-order opinion model represented group interactions beyond pairwise social ties
items.streamSummary: An IEEE model replaces purely pairwise opinion links with group-level hypergraph interactions and derives convergence properties. Its simulated dynamics are not validated human intervention forecasts.
items.attribution: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems — formal opinion-dynamics study

items.streamTitle: Transferred pedestrian models preserved network hierarchy after local calibration
items.streamSummary: A November 2 mobility study transferred behavior models between cities and found persistent network hierarchy after observed-count calibration. Fitted agreement is not an independent prospective test.
items.attribution: Nourmohammadi, Rashidi and Saberi — npj Sustainable Mobility and Transport (transfer/calibration study)

items.streamTitle: Loss and gain framing had opposing effects across retirement-savings subgroups
items.streamSummary: Two retirement-savings experiments (N=22,919 and 18,288) found divergent responses to loss versus gain messages; projected personalized benefits are modeled rather than policy-trial results.
items.attribution: Bösch, Müller, Weinmann and Feuerriegel — Scientific Reports (randomized field experiments)

items.streamTitle: Meaningful AI versioning could make research and audits more reproducible
items.streamSummary: A November 2 Nature Machine Intelligence perspective argues unannounced model changes undermine reproducibility and oversight. Its proposed stronger versioning approach has not been tested for effectiveness.
items.attribution: Mavroudis, Ristea, Morlock and Mougan — Nature Machine Intelligence (Perspective)

items.streamTitle: Low-cost 6-DOF XR tracking sped simulated navigation in a 20-person study
items.streamSummary: A 20-person proof of concept found 6-DOF XR visualization reduced simulated catheter-navigation time and path length relative to 2D guidance. Transfer to other task types remains untested.
items.attribution: Annabestani et al. — npj Biomedical Innovations (engineering proof of concept with human comparison)

items.streamTitle: Friend advice effects varied by adviser status and reciprocal interaction
items.streamSummary: In 66 adult friend dyads, advice valence and adviser relationship status related to mate-choice intention, and a reciprocal model fit best. Neural synchrony was correlational.
items.attribution: Huang et al. — Communications Biology (interactive behavioral study with fNIRS)

items.streamTitle: Graphika found no support for claims Yandex strikes silenced Western political bots
items.streamSummary: After October 7–11 Yandex data-center strikes, Graphika found no unusual loss of activity in the cited Western political communities; viral charts confused web-crawler traffic with bot accounts.
items.attribution: John Kelly / Graphika — original information-environment investigation (October 13)

items.streamTitle: Fixed-rule scientific agent benchmark exposed failures beyond coding mistakes
items.streamSummary: CompMat-Bench used 94 scientific tasks from 15 papers with precomputed simulations; agent accuracy depended on workflow length and guidance. The method has not been validated for behavioral-science automation.
items.attribution: Zhang et al. — arXiv preprint (CompMat-Bench scientific-agent benchmark)

items.streamTitle: Course-integrated AI tutoring reduced grades and engagement in a university trial
items.streamSummary: A 2,379-student randomized university trial found access to an integrated AI tutor reduced grades by 0.37 SD and LMS engagement by 0.90 SD within sections. Mechanisms and generalizability remain uncertain.
items.attribution: Liu et al. — University of Maryland / EdWorkingPapers (randomized university trial)

items.streamTitle: Coordinated AI comments narrowed opinion diversity without increasing average persuasion
items.streamSummary: A 1,000-adult randomized study found coordinated LLM comments compressed opinion diversity by 12% but did not beat independent AI comments in mean persuasion; AI labels changed credibility more than opinion.
items.attribution: Go, Potter, Kim, Ryu and Kim — EMNLP 2026 (randomized human experiment)

items.streamTitle: Structured AI preparation improved reported consultation readiness, not clinical outcomes
items.streamSummary: A randomized 802-person AI preparation study found structured workflows improved clinician-rated and self-rated consultation readiness over a general chatbot. Agreement between those ratings was weak, and actual visit outcomes were not tested.
items.attribution: Tan et al. — arXiv preprint (first-party randomized AI preparation study)

items.streamTitle: Coordinated clarification policy reduced simulated delays when many AI agents shared one supervisor
items.streamSummary: A dynamic-programming model and 864-case synthetic benchmark found a pairwise clarification policy nearly matched optimal cost and cut modeled delay 18–31% versus heuristics. Real human-supervisor benefits remain untested.
items.attribution: Wang, Liu and Wang — arXiv preprint (multi-agent scheduling model)

items.streamTitle: HAIDL-X captured reproducible human–AI notebook interactions, but not validated learning
items.streamSummary: HAIDL-X proposed a notebook interaction schema and demonstrated capture of prompts, code, feedback and execution traces in classroom workflows. It supports auditability but does not establish improved research validity or student learning.
items.attribution: Taufer et al. — arXiv preprint (HAIDL-X research-workflow prototype)

items.streamTitle: Structured AI tutoring improved legal reasoning; programming and retention evidence remained mixed
items.streamSummary: Two preregistered trials found higher immediate legal-reasoning gains with structured AI practice, but no clear four-week retention difference and no significant overall programming advantage. Attrition limits generalization.
items.attribution: AI Cosmos Team / Zhou et al. — arXiv preprint (preregistered randomized learning trials)

items.streamTitle: Competitive rewards produced withdrawal and overinvestment in a 200-agent synthetic society
items.streamSummary: In 200 LLM agents across 50 rounds, low prizes yielded withdrawal while high rewards yielded modeled overcompetition. Widening eligibility changed collective cost and selection. These are synthetic dynamics, not human findings.
items.attribution: Zhao et al. — arXiv preprint (LLM-agent incentive simulation)

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR mapped 146 arms-related information disorders, mostly false claims about weapons flows
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR reviewed 146 conventional-arms information-disorder incidents from 2015–25; three quarters concerned arms flows, often using recycled media. Diplomatic and security effects are plausible but not quantified causally.
items.attribution: Sarah Grand-Clément — UNIDIR (original 40-page incident analysis, October 29)

items.streamTitle: VR eye-and-hand tracking measured distraction costs; richer scenes did not amplify capture
items.streamSummary: A 54-person VR study measured reliable distraction costs in gaze and reaching. More complex scenes increased some overall demands without significantly increasing capture effects, offering a reproducible measurement method rather than evidence of training benefits.
items.attribution: Gurr, Moher, Egbert and Erb — Behavior Research Methods (VR attention experiment)
